assessment_summary:
I validated the installation by inspecting the running environment and exercising the deployed web application over HTTP. The installation method (serve the repo toplevel as nginx document root at /workspace on port 8080) matches the guide's instruction to place config, externalPackages, i18n, src, php and the HTML pages in the webserver document root.

Evidence of completeness and operability: nginx is confirmed running (master PID 1328; `nginx -t` reports success) and serving on :8080. index.html returns 200 with the expected title. Every static asset it references (CSS, JS libraries, ES modules) returns 200 with correct MIME types, and a recursive crawl of the ES-module import graph resolved 25 modules with zero missing files. All guide-required folders (config, externalPackages, i18n, src, php) are served, and the config/i18n JSON files parse correctly. All top-level and example HTML pages, plus their referenced assets, are served successfully, confirming the guide's claim that pages under examples/ are functional where deployed.

Limitations: (1) No browser or JS runtime (node/chromium/firefox) is installed, so end-to-end DOM/JavaScript execution could not be demonstrated; validation is limited to HTTP-level asset resolution and content checks. (2) Elasticsearch — listed as a prerequisite service — is not installed and port 9200 refuses connections, so live index/data querying cannot be exercised; however Elasticsearch is an external backend service, not part of this static web app, and the guide's installation steps cover only deploying the app files. (3) The optional top-level `data/` folder referenced by some KOSIS import configs is absent (those `Satz_Einwohner*` XML samples are gitignored), affecting only optional import workflows.

Given the guide defines the installation as deploying the static HTML/JS application behind a webserver, and that deployment is verified complete and served correctly, the installation is assessed as successful, with the caveats above noted.
